note_on_method: This page covers what we have verified inside Wake County, which is now two of its municipalities and not the rest. Everything below is drawn from the sources listed; where a claim is about the limits of our own coverage rather than about a court, it says so. County assignment is not assumed from the city name — each park was resolved against the US Census Bureau geocoder, because Raleigh is not wholly inside Wake County. This page was rewritten when Cary was added; the previous version said every verified court in the county was inside Raleigh, which stopped being true the day it stopped being true.

slots.coverage: Wake County is the first county in this directory covered by more than one operator. Fourteen parks hold 56 verified outdoor pickleball courts across two municipalities: eleven parks and 44 courts run by Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources, and three parks and 12 courts run by the Town of Cary. Both publish their own court counts, which is the bar a venue has to clear here. Raleigh states each location's count on a single pickleball page and then states the citywide total in prose, and the parts add up to the whole. Cary has no such page and states each count instead in the features list on the facility's own page — "Three pickleball courts" at Ed Yerha, "Basketball & 3 Pickleball Courts" at Carpenter Park — so those counts are published here quoted sentence by sentence. Every park's county was resolved individually rather than assumed from the postcode or the town name: Raleigh straddles a county line, with its Brier Creek area falling inside Durham County, so "a Raleigh park is a Wake County park" needed checking. All fourteen came back Wake, FIPS 37183.
slots.distribution: The courts cluster, and the clustering is the most useful thing to know here. Sanderford Road Park in south-east Raleigh alone holds 10 of the 56, and four more sites hold six apiece — Method Community Park, North Hills Park and Baileywick Park in Raleigh, and the Neighborhood Park on McCrimmon Parkway in north-west Cary. Those five sites account for 34 courts, well over half the county's verified total, at barely a third of its verified locations. The rest is twos and threes: six Raleigh parks with two courts each, Southgate with two, and Cary's Ed Yerha and Carpenter parks with three apiece. Dedicated pickleball is rarer still. Only Method, North Hills and Sanderford Road are permanent pickleball courts in Raleigh's own description, and only McCrimmon is described as lighted pickleball courts by Cary; everywhere else the game is played on lines painted over tennis or basketball. Geographically the set runs from Baileywick in far north Raleigh across to Carpenter Park in north-west Cary and down to Carolina Pines and Sanderford Road in the south.
slots.gaps: Two municipalities is not a county. Apex, Holly Springs, Garner, Wake Forest, Morrisville, Fuquay-Varina, Knightdale, Zebulon and Rolesville are all in Wake County and none of them appears here — not because they have no courts, but because we have not yet found their operators publishing their own court counts, which is the bar everything here has to clear. Inside the two towns we do cover, the gaps are narrower and specific. Two Cary venues are verified in everything but one field and are still not published: Cary Tennis Park, where the town states four lighted pickleball courts and hosts professional tour events, and Middle Creek Community Center, with three indoor courts to rent at $10 an hour. Neither publishes a street address, and a venue does not get a page here without one. We have no verified fee for any of the 56 courts. We have a surface for one of the fourteen sites. And two of Raleigh's counts are disputed between the city's own pickleball page and its own GIS inventory, which we publish rather than quietly resolve.

faqs.q: Does this page cover all of Wake County?
faqs.a: No, and we would rather be plain about it. Everything verified here is inside Raleigh or Cary. Apex, Holly Springs, Garner, Wake Forest, Morrisville, Fuquay-Varina, Knightdale, Zebulon and Rolesville are all in Wake County and none of them appears yet. A town is added when we find its operator publishing its own court counts, not when we find a listing of it somewhere else.

faqs.q: How do you know these parks are in Wake County?
faqs.a: Each park was resolved against the US Census Bureau geocoder — by address where the geocoder matched the street as the town writes it, and otherwise from the coordinates the town itself publishes for that park. All fourteen came back Wake County, FIPS 37183. We check rather than assume because Raleigh crosses a county boundary: the Brier Creek part of the city lies in Durham County, so a rule like "Raleigh means Wake" would be wrong for some Raleigh addresses.

faqs.q: Where are the most courts in Wake County?
faqs.a: Sanderford Road Park in Raleigh, at 10 permanent lit courts, is the largest single site verified in the county. Four sites follow with six each: Method Community Park, North Hills Park and Baileywick Park in Raleigh, and the Neighborhood Park on McCrimmon Parkway in Cary. Those five hold 34 of the county's 56 verified courts between them.

faqs.q: Why is Cary Tennis Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because the Town of Cary publishes no street address for it. The town states the venue has four lighted pickleball courts, it is the best-known racquet facility in the county and it hosts professional tour events — and a venue still does not get a page here without an address, because an address is how a reader finds the place and how we can tell two venues apart. It goes in the day the town publishes one. The same applies to Middle Creek Community Center and its three indoor rental courts.

faqs.q: Is there indoor pickleball in Wake County?
faqs.a: Yes, and almost none of it is verified here. Raleigh Parks runs indoor open play at thirteen community centres at $3 a session or $15 for a four-month pass, and Cary rents three indoor courts at Middle Creek Community Center for $10 an hour per court. Raleigh publishes no court count for any of its thirteen gyms and Cary publishes no address for Middle Creek, so none of them publishes as a venue. We can tell you what indoor play costs in this county; we cannot yet tell you how big it is.

faqs.q: What does verified mean on this page?
faqs.a: That a named source stated the fact and we recorded which source, on what date. For these fourteen parks the court counts, addresses and lighting come from Raleigh Parks, its GIS division and the Town of Cary, and the county from the US Census Bureau. Anything no source stated is left as "Not verified yet" rather than filled in from a plausible guess — which is why you will see far more blanks here than on a directory that infers them.

sources.publisher: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
sources.evidence: States "Raleigh Parks has 44 outdoor pickleball courts located at 11 locations" and tabulates each location with its court count and lighting. Sanderford Road Park 10, Method Community Park 6, North Hills Park 6, Baileywick Park 6, Carolina Pines Park 4, and 2 each at Fred Fletcher, Jaycee, Powell Drive, Roberts, Southgate and Tarboro Road. Method, North Hills and Sanderford Road are marked as permanent courts; the rest are described as tennis or basketball courts with pickleball lines. Fred Fletcher and Southgate are marked unlit. Indoor open play is priced at $3 a session or $15 for a four-month pass across thirteen community centres, with no per-centre court count published.

County resolved for all fourteen parks. Raleigh's eleven and Cary's McCrimmon Parkway park matched by coordinates or address directly; Ed Yerha Park and Carpenter Park did not match by street as the Town of Cary writes them, so their county was resolved from the coordinates the town publishes for each park in its own open data. All fourteen return Wake County, North Carolina, state FIPS 37, county FIPS 183.

sources.publisher: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources, GIS Division
sources.evidence: Athletic Courts feature service. Its per-polygon Pickleball counts agree with E1 at nine of Raleigh's eleven locations and disagree at two: Baileywick, where it gives 4 against E1's 6, and Carolina Pines, where it gives 3 against E1's 4. Its Surface field is populated for Southgate Park only, reading "asphalt", and is empty on every other pickleball polygon in the set.
